newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai authorities probe rubber trading fraud - report.
newsitem.headline: Thai authorities probe rubber trading fraud - report.

text.p: Thailand's Counter Corruption Commission (CCC) is investigating a commerce ministry official in connection with fraudulent trading of government-owned rubber, a Thai newspaper reported on Thursday.
The scam caused about 1.4 billion baht ($53.8 million) in losses for the government, the English-language daily The Nation quoted CCC sources as saying.
Officials at the ministry and the CCC were not available for comment on the report.
The probe, which began a year ago, centered on some irregularities in rubber transactions conducted by the official for the government, the newspaper quoted the sources as saying.
It came to light when unusually large transfers of money were made during transaction periods, the sources said.
Some rubber is believed to have been sold from government stocks to brokers instead of direct buyers as required under the regulations.
But the buyers could not be identified and the destinations of the rubber consignments were unknown.
More rubber was contracted for sale than was held in stocks by the state-run Rubber Estate Organization, and at low prices, causing the government to suffer losses, the sources said.
